hypothesis: A pitcher current-season success rate loses information about why control failed. Reconstructing the row-local success/reverse/middle/wide mixture from official as-of counters and using it as a multinomial probability offset should let stable count and matchup effects transfer without a high-variance tree residual.

legality.historical_outcome_recovery: next-row counter differences are used only inside the strictly earlier training slice; boundary rows are dropped

fixed_recipe.route: R only; every F prediction remains the comparison baseline
fixed_recipe.success_prior: two-level pitcher posterior: completed-history EB k=1000, current-season EB k=80
fixed_recipe.failure_mix_prior: current-season reverse/middle/remaining-wide rates, EB k=80, normalized inside 1-success
fixed_recipe.model: zero-initialized additive four-class PyTorch lookup/linear model with the reconstructed log probabilities as a fixed offset

selection.eligibility: positive R point gain and positive pitcher-cluster 95% R gain lower bound in every development-year/comparison cell
selection.ranking: largest minimum R point gain across all cells, then smaller gamma
selection.failure_rule: if no gamma is eligible, do not fit or read a 2024 candidate

confirmation.completion: V5 validation contract v2 conservative lower score and all package gates
